_comment: Reference sequences and bioactive motifs for sequence-based function inference. Every entry requires verification against UniProt or primary literature before being relied on — this is a local cache, not an authority. Sequences here are included only where they are well established; where a sequence was uncertain it was left out rather than approximated, because a wrong sequence produces confidently wrong downstream analysis.

GLP-1(7-37).function: Incretin hormone: glucose-dependent insulin secretion, satiety, gastric emptying delay via GLP-1R
GLP-1(7-37).goal_reason: Native GLP-1 has a circulating half-life of roughly two minutes due to DPP-4 cleavage at position 2. Protease resistance is the dominant liability for this scaffold.

Glucagon.function: Counter-regulatory hormone: raises blood glucose via GCGR
Glucagon.goal_reason: Shares the DPP-4-susceptible N-terminus of the glucagon superfamily.

Insulin A-chain.function: A-chain of insulin; disulfide-linked to the B-chain in the mature hormone
Insulin A-chain.goal_reason: An isolated chain is not the functional unit. The cysteines here form interchain disulfides, so this is a fragment of a binary complex rather than a standalone peptide.

Insulin B-chain.function: B-chain of insulin; carries the receptor-binding surface
Insulin B-chain.goal_reason: Carries the primary receptor-binding determinants, but only in the disulfide-linked complex with the A-chain.

Oxytocin.function: Uterine contraction, milk ejection, social bonding via OXTR
Oxytocin.goal_reason: Short cyclic peptide with a very short plasma half-life; exposure is the limiting property.

Vasopressin.function: Antidiuresis and vasoconstriction via V1/V2 receptors
Vasopressin.goal_reason: Short half-life; desmopressin is the clinical precedent for stabilising this scaffold.

Substance P.function: Neurokinin-1 receptor agonist: pain transmission, neurogenic inflammation
Substance P.goal_reason: Rapidly degraded by neprilysin and ACE; the C-terminal Met is also an oxidation liability.

Bradykinin.function: Vasodilation, vascular permeability, pain via B2 receptor
Bradykinin.goal_reason: Half-life under a minute; degraded by ACE and neprilysin.

LL-37.function: Cathelicidin host-defence peptide: membrane-disrupting antimicrobial, immunomodulatory
LL-37.goal_reason: Cationic amphipathic helix. Activity depends on the amphipathic fold, so constraint moves and protease resistance both apply; salt sensitivity is the other classic liability.

BPC-157.function: Synthetic pentadecapeptide derived from a gastric juice protein fragment; reported in tissue-repair models
BPC-157.goal_reason: Human clinical evidence is limited. Reported stability in gastric juice is the distinguishing claim for this peptide, so proteolytic behaviour is the property most worth examining.

IKVAV.location: LG domain region of the alpha-1 chain
IKVAV.function: Neurite outgrowth, cell adhesion and migration; widely used to functionalise scaffolds for neural regeneration
IKVAV.goal_reason: A short adhesion motif excised from a very large basement-membrane protein. Its activity is presentation-dependent — density, spacing and multivalency dominate — so binding and its structural context matter more than half-life.
IKVAV.native_context_note: This is an internal fragment of a multi-thousand-residue ECM protein. Both termini are excision artefacts, and in the native protein the motif is displayed on a folded domain rather than as a free peptide.

YIGSR.location: Domain III of the beta-1 chain
YIGSR.function: Cell adhesion via the 67 kDa laminin receptor; reported anti-metastatic and anti-angiogenic activity
YIGSR.goal_reason: Adhesion motif whose activity depends on receptor engagement and presentation rather than circulating exposure.
YIGSR.native_context_note: Internal fragment of laminin beta-1. Free termini are excision artefacts.

RKRLQVQLSIRT.parent_protein: Laminin alpha-1 chain, LG4 module (the peptide commonly designated AG73)
RKRLQVQLSIRT.function: Syndecan-binding; cell adhesion, spreading and neurite outgrowth
RKRLQVQLSIRT.goal_reason: Heparin/syndecan binding is charge-driven, so charge engineering and presentation dominate over proteolytic stability.
RKRLQVQLSIRT.native_context_note: Internal fragment of the laminin alpha-1 LG4 module; strongly cationic, which is the basis of its syndecan binding.

RGD.parent_protein: Integrin-binding motif found in fibronectin, vitronectin, and several other matrix proteins
RGD.goal_reason: Integrin selectivity depends almost entirely on the conformation the RGD is presented in — cyclic RGD peptides differ from linear ones by orders of magnitude in both affinity and integrin subtype selectivity.
RGD.native_context_note: A three-residue motif is too short to be specific on its own. Flanking residues and conformational constraint determine which integrin it engages.
RGD.min_length_warning: RGD alone is only three residues. A match here indicates the motif is present, not that the peptide's function is adhesion.

family_signatures._comment: Physicochemical signatures used when no sequence or motif match is found. These are heuristics over computed Tier 0 properties and are reported as INFERRED, never as identification.

cationic_amphipathic_amp.description: Cationic amphipathic helix — the host-defence / antimicrobial peptide profile
cationic_amphipathic_amp.goal_reason: Antimicrobial peptides are typically protease-labile and lose activity on proteolysis. Activity also depends on the amphipathic fold, so constraint moves are the other productive direction.

disulfide_rich.description: Disulfide-rich scaffold — defensin, knottin, or growth-factor-like fold
disulfide_rich.goal_reason: Disulfide-rich scaffolds are already proteolytically stable because of their crosslinked fold, so protease resistance is rarely the limiting property. Binding and correct disulfide pairing dominate.

collagen_like.goal_reason: Gly/Pro-rich sequences are MMP and collagenase substrates.
